regras.t: Step 1 to learn a rank: stable your main pet before you tame the donor.
Step 2: tame the donor beast, a wild creature at the level and zone listed for that rank.
Step 3: with the donor out, turn off its other abilities and fight until the new skill is learned.
Step 4: once the skill is learned, let the donor go, since donor pets should be kept only as long as needed.
Step 5: take your main pet out of the stable and train the skill on it at Beast Training.
Every family can learn Bite or Claw, sometimes both, plus Dash or Dive. Those ranks never upgrade on their own: you must learn and teach each new one.
Beast Training is in the General tab of the spellbook, not in the Beast Mastery tab.
You can skip ranks: a pet that meets the level for rank 4 does not need to learn rank 1 first.
Beast Lore unlocks at level 24 and lets you inspect a wild beast's skills before you tame it.
A pet trainer teaches Growl, Great Stamina, Natural Armor and resistances; damage attacks, movement and many family skills come from temporary donor tames.
Growl costs no training points but still takes one of the four active ability slots.
A newly tamed low-level pet needs experience to catch up, so keep stable space free for the skills you still need to learn.
Food closer to the pet's level works better, and each family eats only some foods, so check its diet before buying stock.
Claw has no cooldown and can spend focus fast, so cast a control skill like Web by hand when timing matters instead of letting the pet spend it all.
Pets now scale with your hunter gear: attack power, armor, stamina, hit and crit all feed the pet, so upgrading your own gear makes it stronger too.
Blizzard says pets are less durable than intended and plans a stat adjustment on November 10; the numbers are unconfirmed, so doubt tanky picks for now.
At level 10, finishing both parts of the taming quest unlocks feeding and Beast Training. Busy players should tame something nearby, close to level 10.
Early pet by race (level range): Human Prowler (9-10, Elwynn Forest); Dwarf Scarred Crag Boar (9-10, Dun Morogh); Orc/Troll Elder Mottled Boar (9-10, Durotar).
Night Elf Elder Nightsaber (about level 8, Teldrassil); Tauren Taloned Swoop (Mulgore) and Skyborne Windsong Crawler (Zephras Isle), no level given.
Keep a usable rank of Bite or Claw as your first priority.
Corehounds appear in some game data, but the speaker has not verified a tameable one on Forever, so do not plan a build around them.
Humar, Spiteflayer and Deathmaw are known for looks or attack interval, not guaranteed PvE damage; do not camp a rare for hours.
A family damage modifier is not a damage meter result: focus, attack abilities, uptime and fight length change the outcome.
The first raids open on December 9, so raid DPS rankings are not settled and any raid pet pick is provisional.
Common mistakes: skipping feeding, forgetting to teach new ranks, and leaving Growl on when another player is tanking.
Dismiss your pet before dangerous dungeon jumps, and do not chase every donor you see; pick only the upgrades you will actually use.
Training points equal pet level times (loyalty minus 1), and buying a higher rank refunds the points of the lower one.
A pet can have four active abilities, while passive abilities have no cap.
Stable slots: the first is free, the second costs 10 silver and the third 5 gold; LudiDeo says Blizzard promised more.
Happy pets deal 125% damage, content 100% and unhappy 75%, so feed them often to keep happiness up.
A rank has two levels: PET LVL is the minimum for your pet, BEAST LVL is the wild teacher you tame. Keep your own pet; the teacher is only borrowed.
Blizzard's 24/09 beta notes: Tame Beast stopped working on beasts above your level.
Same-family pets have normalized basic damage, so faster attacks hit weaker each time; speed can still matter for PvP pushback.
Attack speed is normalized, so damage on paper is the same; a faster pet only gains on procs, such as Frenzy.
Frenzy depends on pet speed; 3 points suit a 1.0 pet like Broken Tooth, while 1.2 sits at the limit.
Blizzard's 03/11 beta notes: a pet no longer loses its inherent attack speed passive when it is untrained.
Rare pets are optional and not automatic PvE upgrades, though some, such as Broken Tooth at 1.0 seconds, attack fast.

notas.t: Tier (LudiDeo): leveling S, PvP A.
+10% family damage, with Prowl as its signature ability; its best use is damage.
Its pick for fast everyday kills and fast leveling, with Raptor as the other damage option.
Offensive family with +10% damage, Claw and Bite, at the top for damage together with the raptor.
The cat is the pick for damage-focused leveling and for end-game PvE, before the raptor.
On a Night Elf he runs a nightsaber with Bite.
Broken Tooth, a level 37 Cat in Badlands with 1.0s attacks, is known as a PvP cat.
Leveling S: damage is king, with Bite, Claw and Prowl. PvP A because Prowl gives a strong opener, though he says it is not S in PvP.
Diet is simple (meat). He gives no number that would change either letter.
Tier (LudiDeo): leveling A, PvP B.
+10% family damage, with Savage Rend as its signature ability; a damage family.
Close to the cat, with more armor and less health, at the top for damage.
A damage alternative to the cat for dungeons; its raid ranking is still provisional.
Listed with the cat for stronger damage in levels 31 to 40 and for damage-focused leveling.
Savage Rend is a bleed that pays off when the enemy lives long enough to tick; the raptor stays a serious alternative to the cat on longer fights.
Second best DPS after cat, a weaker cat with Rend (18 s bleed, 50 focus, 1 min cooldown). PvP held back by the bleed and the cooldown.
What would change: with a 30 s cooldown on Rend he says it would be A in PvP.
Tier (LudiDeo): leveling B*, PvP B. (* no letter given; read from his words)
+7% family damage plus Lightning Breath; its best use is nature damage.
Among the defensive-damage families, with bat, bird of prey and spider.
Leveling B is a reading of his words: average solid pet, no downside, nothing crazy. PvP B is explicit, for its 20 yard range.
He gives no number that would change either list.
Tier (LudiDeo): leveling A*, PvP C. (* no letter given; read from his words)
Its signature ability is Scorpid Poison, and its best use is poison.
A tank family with low damage, so holding threat is hard.
For Horde leveling against one target, the scorpid is the pick for a long fight.
Leveling A is a reading of his words: second best single target tank, better than bore in long fights as poison stacks to 125 damage at five.
PvP C is explicit: the only value is the poison, and it is a low-damage tank.
Tier (LudiDeo): leveling A, PvP C*. (* no letter given; read from his words)
Its overall pick for a first pet, sturdy and accessible, with Charge as its signature.
Scarred Crag Boar in Dun Morogh for Dwarf; Elder Mottled Boar in Durotar for Orc and Troll.
The single-target tank for leveling, because Charge holds the threat.
A boar's Charge lets you jump with Bestial Swiftness.
Charge closes the distance, briefly holds the target and strengthens the next hit; boars eat many foods, so they are easy to feed.
Leveling A is explicit: Charge gives the most threat of any pet, so it is great for leveling. No Claw keeps it from S.
PvP C is a reading of his words: he calls the boar slightly better than bear (D), not on the level of the top PvP pets.
The safer solo pick for low-stress leveling, with Demoralizing Screech as its signature.
A balanced family, with Claw and Bite.
Demoralizing Screech no longer generates area threat since the beta.
Takes a carrion bird for survival, and uses Demoralizing Screech so the pet takes less damage.
Spiteflayer, a fast Carrion Bird at level 52 in Blasted Lands, is a rare option.
The best two-pet combo is a Cat with a Carrion Bird, for strong damage and forgiving solo play.
Demoralizing Screech damages the enemy and lowers the melee attack power of nearby enemies, which helps when several mobs hit you.
Strongest A in leveling. Demoralize was nerfed (it used to hold several targets), and it does less damage than the top PvP pets.
Ambiguous: at the end he thinks about S in leveling, then says no tank deserves S. Not decided; kept at A.
Tier (LudiDeo): leveling A, PvP D.
The multi-target pick, with Gorilla as the alternative.
The area-farming pick, since Swipe hits 3 targets on a 5 second cooldown.
Swipe Rank 1 comes from Grizzled Black Bear in Loch Modan, or Giant Grizzled Bear in Silverpine.
For Human and Dwarf in levels 11 to 20, look for a nearby boar, bear or cat.
Sturdier than most families, and its Swipe hits three nearby enemies, which suits area pulls.
A bear or gorilla is a utility pick, not a proven threat ranking; test threat side by side before relying on it.
Leveling A is explicit: Swipe multitanks up to three targets, but the -9 percent damage modifier keeps it from S.
PvP D is explicit: pretty bad in PvP, with nothing for it there. He says it would be S without the low damage modifiers.
Tier (LudiDeo): leveling B, PvP C.
An AoE utility family with Thunderstomp, and the alternative to Bear for multi-target.
Thunderstomp Rank 1 comes from Mistvale Gorilla, level 32 to 33 in Stranglethorn Vale.
Grouped with the tanks, with low damage.
Like the bear, it is not proven as the best AoE tank; test threat with both side by side before choosing one.
Thunderstomp hits all enemies, but its 1 min cooldown, with aggro lasting about 20 s, holds it at B. No Claw either.
With a 20 s cooldown he says A, maybe S; with 30 s, A. PvP C is explicit, for its use in revealing a rogue.
Tier (LudiDeo): leveling C*, PvP D*. (* no letter given; read from his words)
A strong defensive option, excellent against hard-hitting enemies and tough solo targets.
Shell Shield Rank 1 is donated by Kresh, level 20, in Wailing Caverns.
The pick for a very heavy elite solo, since Shell Shield cuts damage taken by 50%.
Both letters are a reading of his words: 'it has a use over the crab' for leveling, and 'in PvP, nothing' for PvP.
Viable with a 1 minute cooldown instead of 3, he says. He also thinks it needs a buff.
Tier (LudiDeo): leveling S, PvP S*. (* no letter given; read from his words)
The PvP control pick; Web roots runners for control and kiting.
Web Rank 1 comes from Moss Stalker in Silverpine or Cliff Lurker in Loch Modan, levels 12 to 14.
A balanced family, with Web rooting for 4 seconds.
Leveling S is explicit: a 4 s root with 40 s cooldown and low focus, with no downside beyond no Claw.
PvP S is a reading of his words: he calls the root amazing in PvP, with no question about it, but gives no letter.
Tier (LudiDeo): leveling D*, PvP C. (* no letter given; read from his words)
For Skyborne characters, a crab first, then upgrades chosen by role.
Pinch slows movement for chasing or escape, and is listed with the hyena for kiting.
Leveling D is a reading of his words: he says the crab is the worst pet in the game for him, with no value beyond armor.
PvP C is explicit: a slow (Pinch, 50 percent for 9 s, 30 s cooldown), but he says the kit already has many slows.
Tier (LudiDeo): leveling B, PvP B.
Its signature ability is Tendon Rip, a bleed with a slow.
A balanced family, along with the wolf and the fox.
Tendon Rip is listed with the crab for kiting, as a movement slow.
Tendon Rip: same slow as Pinch with a 9 s bleed at half the focus (25). Slightly less damage, but he says the bleed is a win.
Would be S in PvP without the slows and bleed already in the kit, he says.
Tier (LudiDeo): leveling A, PvP S.
A healing-reduction pick; Dismember cuts healing by 25% for 6 seconds, for PvP against healers.
A tank family with low damage; in PvP, Dismember acts as a 25% mortal strike against healers.
Kargoz (beta) names the crocolisk as his pet, used with Mortal Strike.
Leveling A: no damage penalty, very high armor and Dismember; mobs with heals (shamans) make its healing cut useful in leveling.
PvP S is explicit: Dismember cuts healing (he says 25 percent), and he says there is no question about it.
The anti-caster pick, with Sonic Blast slowing enemy casting; plan around its cooldown.
A defensive-damage family, and the pick for PvP against casters.
PvP S is explicit: a 20 s undispellable effect against healers, locks and mages. Leveling A: Sonic Blast is weak in the open world.
Diet is picky (fungus, fruit), which he counts against it. He names no value that would make it S in leveling.
Tier (LudiDeo): leveling C, PvP A.
Blizzard (30/09): the Owl became the Bird of Prey.
Its signature ability is Mine!, a 3 second disarm on a 90 second cooldown, used against melee.
A defensive-damage family, and the pick for PvP against melee.
Leveling C is explicit: Mine (3 s disarm) is one of the worst specials for leveling, and owls are hard to find.
PvP A is explicit: Claw is strong in PvP, and the disarm has a niche. He gives no number that would change either list.
Its signature ability is Dust Cloud, which reduces armor.
For Tauren in levels 11 to 20, the routes are Carrion Bird or Tallstrider.
Dust Cloud (1.3 s) cuts enemy armor. Solid with no downside beyond no Claw. It does not stack with Faerie Fire.
PvP B is explicit: armor reduction is good against squishy mages. He gives no number that would change either list.
Melee support through Furious Howl, an optional group pick for suitable melee groups.
A survival pick, since Furious Howl is a battle shout for the hunter.
Deathmaw, a fast Wolf, is a rare level 53 pet in Burning Steppes.
Furious Howl was nerfed during beta and does not stack with Battle Shout, so check what the group already has before bringing a wolf.
Leveling: S if you play Survival, A otherwise (his end-of-video condition). Furious Howl is a battle shout; no Claw.
PvP B is explicit: just an average pet, with no strong value in PvP.
Tier (LudiDeo): leveling D*, PvP B. (* no letter given; read from his words)
Blizzard (30/09): Fox is a new family, and its special ability is Trickster's Dance.
A dodge and speed family; its niche upgrade path uses Gray Fox in Duskwood.
A balanced family, along with the hyena and the wolf.
Leveling D is a reading of his words: 'I don't see a value' with current stats and a 3 min cooldown on Trickster's Dance. PvP B is explicit.
He says maybe S with rank 2 or 3 (100 percent dodge at max rank, 50 percent attack speed), or sure with a 30 s cooldown.

Savage Rend.t: Raptor bleed that is more useful when the enemy survives long enough to tick; rank 1 comes from the Sunscale Screecher in the Barrens.

Trickster's Dance.t: Fox skill that improves dodge and attack speed for a short time; rank 1 comes from the Gray Fox in Duskwood.

Dive.t: Some families learn Dive in place of Dash; both are movement skills that improve pet uptime.

Claw.t: On a cat, turn Claw autocast off and use Bite on its cooldown, which LudiDeo says gives 1 to 2% more damage.

Bite.t: Claw costs 25 focus with no cooldown; Bite costs 35 focus with a 10 second cooldown and almost double the damage.

Growl.t: Growl costs no training points. Keep its rank current for solo play; in groups with a tank, turn it off.

Cower.t: In groups, leave Cower on to reduce threat, while Growl goes off.

Mend Pet.t: Use Mend Pet before things get risky, and early rather than late.

Dash.t: Dash and Dive improve pet uptime noticeably; Saltii puts Dash or Dive around level 30.

Swipe.t: Swipe hits 3 targets on a 5 second cooldown, so it suits farming in an area.

Thunderstomp.t: Do not break crowd control with Swipe or Thunderstomp.

Web.t: Web roots the target for control and kiting, and suits PvP against runners.

Pinch.t: Pinch slows movement, for chasing or for escape.

Dismember.t: Dismember cuts healing by 25% for 6 seconds, which suits PvP against healers.

Mine!.t: Mine! disarms a melee target for 3 seconds, on a 90 second cooldown.

Sonic Blast.t: Sonic Blast slows enemy casting, so plan around its cooldown.

Furious Howl.t: Furious Howl is a battle shout for the hunter, which makes the wolf a survival pick.

Shell Shield.t: Shell Shield cuts damage taken by 50%, which suits a very heavy elite solo.

Demoralizing Screech.t: Gladius uses Demoralizing Screech so the pet takes less damage.

Charge.t: A boar's Charge lets you jump with Bestial Swiftness.

Beast Lore.t: Use Beast Lore before a long tame trip, to inspect the beast's skills.

Prowl.t: On a Night Elf, a cat with Prowl is a PvP option.
